rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. This configuration tests the simplest setup (rna_only with singleprofile and PCA encoder) to compare against more complex models. It isolates the effect of RNA encoding and profile setting, providing foundational performance metrics before exploring multimodal or advanced aggregation/fusion methods.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation. It directly addresses whether multiprofile (a key design choice) improves performance compared to singleprofile, while keeping RNA encoder and fusion methods constant. This clarifies the importance of profile setting and aggregation, balancing exploration of critical factors with minimal changes from the baseline.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile (config_002) outperforms singleprofile (config_001) with RNA-only models using avgpool aggregation. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from PCA_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more complex model) improves performance while keeping profile_setting=multiprofile and aggregation=avgpool. This isolates the effect of the RNA encoder choice, which is critical for understanding whether more sophisticated encoders yield gains. It balances exploration (testing a new encoder) with exploitation (building on the multiprofile advantage).

Existing evidence shows multiprofile setups (config_002/005) outperform singleprofile, and scvi_n200 (config_005) is better than pca_n2000. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation (vs avgpool in config_005) further improves performance with scvi_n200 in multiprofile, isolating the impact of aggregation method. It balances exploration of key design choices (aggregation) while building on proven components (scvi_n200, multiprofile).

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings and transformer aggregation improve performance. This experiment tests whether using the scgpt RNA encoder (instead of scvi_n200) in the same multiprofile setup with transformer aggregation can further improve accuracy, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder choice. It balances exploration of encoder impact with exploitation of known beneficial design choices.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 with avgpool aggregation (config_005) outperforms pca_n2000 with avgpool (config_002). This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation improves performance for pca_n2000 in multiprofile settings, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It addresses uncertainty about whether transformer aggregation is beneficial for lower-performing encoders like pca_n2000, providing insights into the interplay between encoder choice and aggregation strategy.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether adding image data (multimodal) with the same RNA encoder and aggregation method can improve performance, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploitation of the best RNA-only setup with exploration of multimodal potential, addressing a key design choice without changing multiple variables.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, and transformer aggregation achieve high performance (config_032: 0.6878 accuracy). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from concat to weighted (while keeping other components constant) improves performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, and builds on the strong foundation of the current top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more complex image encoder) further improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice while keeping other components consistent.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (while keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion the same) improves performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder. This is critical for understanding if more complex encoders outperform simpler ones in this context.
